scope: Five-minute Android Chrome mobile Web background/resume check with a listener-only Android receiver and an independent synthetic browser sender. RTP counters advanced after return. This is not Flutter microphone acceptance or proof of audible output.

environment.sender: Playwright Chromium with synthetic microphone input
environment.qa_server: Owned disposable API/PostgreSQL/LiveKit QA stack; no production service

scenario.receiver_mode: Android Chrome voice listener with microphone disabled
scenario.background_action: Android Home; Chrome DevTools Protocol detached for the full interval

media_counters.result: RTP packet and byte counters advanced after resume; the same single peer connection remained active.

visual_review.observation: At source resolution, Android Chrome showed two voice participants, a connected status, the mobile-browser background limitation notice, and the voice controls. No obvious rendering defect was observed in this capture.

limitations: The sender used synthetic Playwright audio; it was not the Flutter Android microphone.
RTP packet and byte counters do not prove decoded samples reached a speaker or were audible to a person; no acoustic loopback or human listening test was performed.
This is a five-minute emulator result, not physical Android acceptance or the physical paired 60-minute gate.
The screen was backgrounded to Android Home; secure keyguard lock was not exercised.
No Wi-Fi/LTE switch, airplane mode, process kill, permission revoke, battery saver, Safari/PWA, iOS audio session, production release, or production smoke was tested.
Issue #785 remains open; this scoped result does not close the release gate.
